fields.h1: Build Business Travel Survey Questions for Every Trip
fields.hero_description: Build business travel survey questions that go out after each trip, rate every leg, and save answers to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Travel Survey
fields.features_subheading: One prompt builds the survey and the table behind it. A later prompt changes the questions before the next trip goes out.
fields.feature_1:
One question set per leg of the trip

List the legs to rate, such as booking, the flight, the hotel, and ground transport. Emergent drafts a 1 to 5 rating and a comment box for each, and a prompt rewords any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Sent the day after a trip ends

The app reads each trip's return date from your booking tool through its API and sends the survey the next day. A traveler back from a 3-day trip answers while the hotel is fresh.
fields.feature_3:
Destination and cost center on each answer

Each response is a row in a database you own, tagged with destination, hotel, trip purpose, and cost center. Sort hotel scores by city, or compare one team's answers by quarter.
fields.feature_4:
Low hotel scores go to the travel manager

Pick the score that needs a reply. When a traveler rates a hotel 1 or 2 out of 5, the app sends the travel manager a Slack message with the hotel name and the traveler's comment.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen, on any phone

Travelers answer one question per screen on a phone, in a taxi or at the gate. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so every traveler at a 900-person firm can answer after every trip.
fields.feature_6:
A domain and a codebase of your own

Run the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and paid for in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and track every change there.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Companies Use Travel Surveys
fields.tab_content_1:
Fenwick Lodge is out in Denver, with 7 scores of 1 or 2

Kessock Engineering surveys each traveler the day after they return, with a rating per leg. In October, 84 of 112 travelers answered. Of the 9 who stayed at Fenwick Lodge in Denver, 7 rated the hotel 1 or 2, and each score sent travel manager Lisandra Muirhead a Slack message. She took the lodge off the booking list.
fields.tab_content_2:
The Boston hotel cap rose $75 when 61 travelers called it low

Once a year, Brisbourne Biotech asks its 140 travelers about the travel policy itself, one city cap at a time. This year 118 answered, and 61 of them said the $250 nightly hotel cap was too low for Boston. Finance controller Cassiel Prentice raised the Boston cap to $325 and kept the other cities at $250.
fields.tab_content_3:
Renewal visits that could have been a video call

After each customer visit, a Quillmore Software account rep answers 3 questions, and the last one asks whether a video call would have done the job. Over the summer quarter, reps said yes for 26 of 74 visits, and 21 of those 26 were renewals. VP of sales Avelline Delacourt now opens every renewal with a video call.
fields.tab_content_4:
Chicago gets one preferred hotel, chosen by 152 travelers

Vantry Logistics wanted one preferred hotel near its Chicago office and let its travelers choose. The survey listed 4 hotels within a 10-minute walk, and 152 travelers voted. Bexwell Suites took 71 votes to 44 for Hadleigh Court. Travel coordinator Ambrose Kearsley asked Bexwell Suites for a negotiated nightly rate.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Travel Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write business travel survey questions that travelers finish after each trip and that show what to change.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the trips that get a survey
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Give each leg its own question
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask whether the trip was worth it
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Save policy questions for once a year
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide which trips get a survey before you write a question. Overnight trips make a clean line, since a day trip has no hotel to rate. Put that rule in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the survey around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about each leg of the trip separately, on the same 1 to 5 scale. One overall score hides whether the flight or the hotel went wrong. With a single scale, a Denver hotel and a Boston hotel compare directly.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add one question on the outcome: did the trip do what it was for? For client and sales visits, ask if a phone or video meeting could have replaced it. Those answers show which trips to keep booking.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Questions about the travel policy itself, such as hotel caps or class of service, belong in a separate yearly survey. Mixed into every post-trip survey, they make it longer and collect the same answer trip after trip.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Hold the post-trip survey to 8 questions or fewer, so a traveler can finish it on the ride home. Skip anything the booking record already holds, like dates and the airline. Attach those details to each answer instead.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Name who reads the low scores
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose a score that calls for action, such as a hotel rated 1 or 2, and name one person to read it. A travel manager who sees a bad hotel score the day it comes in can pull that hotel before the next booking.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run it with one team first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send the survey to one department for a month before anyone else gets it. Read every answer, reword any question people skip, and check that trip details land on each response. Then turn it on for every traveler.

faq_plan.q: What are business travel survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Business travel survey questions are what a company asks employees about work trips: how the flight and hotel rated, and whether the trip met its goal. Post-trip questions go out after each trip. Questions about the travel policy, such as whether hotel caps fit, suit a yearly survey.

faq_plan.q: How do I create business travel survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Describe the survey in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: which trips get it, the legs to rate, and who hears about a low score. Emergent builds the survey and the database behind it, and a follow-up prompt edits any question before the first traveler sees it.

faq_plan.q: What business travel survey questions work best after a trip?
faq_plan.a: Ask about the trip they took, in plain words: how would you rate the hotel, 1 to 5? Did the car or train from the airport show up on time? Was the trip worth the time away? Close with one open question, such as what should change before the next trip to this city.

faq_plan.q: How often should a company send business travel survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Send the post-trip survey after every qualifying trip and the policy survey once a year. For people who travel every week, cap it at one post-trip survey a month. Past that, the questions start to feel like a chore and get skipped.

faq_plan.q: Should answers to business travel survey questions be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Not for post-trip surveys, since an answer is only useful tied to the trip and the hotel. For a travel policy review, anonymous answers suit questions about caps and rules. Say which kind each survey is in the invitation, and keep that promise.

faq_plan.q: Which business travel survey questions test the travel policy?
faq_plan.a: Ask whether each hotel cap fits the cities people visit, whether the booking rules leave enough choice, and whether trip approval came in time. Ask about one city or rule at a time. A low score then points to one line of the policy. Each answer lands in a database you own, with this year's results beside last year's.

faq_plan.q: Which business travel survey questions show if a trip was worth it?
faq_plan.a: Two questions cover it: did the trip meet its goal, and what is the agreed next step? For client visits, add whether a call could have replaced the visit. Count those answers by trip type each quarter, and the pattern shows which trips to keep booking.

faq_plan.q: How do you get more employees to answer business travel survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Send it the day after the trip, while the details are fresh, and keep it short. Then show travelers what their answers changed, such as a hotel taken off the booking list. The survey Emergent builds shows one question per screen, which suits a traveler answering on a phone.

faq_plan.q: How do you act on low hotel scores in business travel survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Read the comment before acting. A broken heater is a one-off, while a hotel far from the client office will disappoint on every stay. Raise one-off problems with the hotel, and drop a hotel from the booking list once low scores repeat across several stays.

faq_plan.q: Can business travel survey questions pull trip details from a booking tool?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the booking tool has an API. The app Emergent builds can read each trip's dates and hotel through that API and attach them to the answer. Travelers never type those details; they see only questions about how the trip went.
